title: Stream-first JSON fallback assertor and compatibility scenarios
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Build a focused test harness and assertor that validates graceful fallback behavior when enforcing JSON-mode / constrained decoding in streaming responses. This ticket scopes tests that exercise partial-stream emits, KV cache replays, tool/function-call interleaving, and decoder backpressure to ensure schema adherence or safe fallback (plain-text summary + structured error) without breaking live connections or mis-attributing tokens to downstream tool calls.
background: We have recurring incidents where strict schema enforcement in streaming causes long-lived requests to either hang (decoder stalls) or emit malformed toolcall boundaries when prefix cache is replayed. Existing testbeds exercise static full-response decodes; we need stream-first scenarios that interleave tool calls, KV cache warm-starts, and token-level backpressure to replicate production edgecases seen in customers running long chat sessions with function/tool invocations.
scope: Create a harness that can: (1) drive multi-chunk streaming responses with configurable token delays; (2) inject KV cache replay mid-stream; (3) simulate function/tool call tokens arriving mid-output; (4) assert schema conformance at incremental checkpoints and verify fallback emission when strict decoding fails; (5) produce telemetry for token-level attribution and replay traces.
out_of_scope: Changes to runtime kernel selection or model packaging. Production rollout policies — this ticket focuses on testing and assertor logic only.
acceptance_criteria: A harness that can replay a historical 45-token prefix then continue streaming with injected delay patterns

At least 6 deterministic test scenarios covering: clean schema succeed, partial-token-split at JSON boundary, KV replay collision, interleaved toolcall tokens, beam-prune-induced truncation, and backpressure-triggered partial-emit

When strict JSON enforcement fails mid-stream, the assertor produces a single, well-formed fallback envelope: {"fallback":true, "reason": <short code>, "summary": <short text>}, followed by connection close or graceful completion per scenario
Telemetry emitted for each test with token-attribution mapping (source: model|cache|tool) and a failure classification string
Automated CI job that runs the harness against two model variants (open-1.3b-quant, open-7b-raw) and returns non-zero on regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for assertor logic (token boundary detector, fallback envelope formatter)
Integration harness that spins up streaming server mock + decoder shim to simulate partial outputs
Chaos scenarios with randomized token delays seeded for reproducibility
Golden-file comparisons for fallback envelopes and telemetry payloads
Performance baseline: harness should run 1000 scenario permutations in < 30m on CI runner
implementation_notes: Implement assertor as a small standalone binary (golang) to avoid Python GIL bottlenecks when simulating thousands of delayed tokens
Use existing KV cache replay fixture (ENG-14266) but extend to support mid-stream injection points
Leverage streaming test runner from infra/tests/stream-mock in repo: will add adapter to emit toolcall sentinel tokens '<TOOLCALL_START>' / '<TOOLCALL_END>'
Fallback envelope schema is intentionally minimal to be consumable by SDKs: {fallback:true, reason:string, summary:string, meta:map<string>} — meta will be flattened in telemetry
Add a small feature flag 'stream_json_assertor' to enable harness-only codepaths in staging clusters for manual canaries
comments: 2026-02-11: Aisha Raman - Kickoff: sketched test matrix with SRE and runtime; primary risk is non-deterministic token timing in CI. Decided to seed random delays to make failures reproducible.

2026-02-18: Tomás Delgado - Spike complete: implemented prototype stream mock that can pause/resume at token boundaries. Found an edge where tokenization splits braces across two tokens leading to false-negative schema checks; added token-boundary normalizer.

2026-02-24: Reviewer (Ellen Park) - Feedback: ensure fallback envelope contains short machine-readable reason codes (e.g., 'KV_COLLIDE', 'TOOL_BOUNDARY', 'TRUNCATION') and include original request id for traceability. Also asked to add a test that simulates partial network reconnects.

2026-03-03: Tomás Delgado - Added mid-stream KV replay scenario. Observed that when replayed prefix is longer than model context warm-up threshold, decoder emits repeated tokens. Mitigation: mark replay source in token attribution and treat repeated prefix as a soft-failure rather than strict schema violation.

2026-03-09: Aisha Raman - Integration PR opened (infra #1842). Devs: please review the fallback envelope formatter and CI job config. Need SRE sign-off for running these heavier harness tests in daily CI.

2026-03-14: Synthesize: we have 5/6 scenarios green on prototype models; beam-prune truncation case still flaky on open-7b-raw. Plan: add deterministic beam pruning seeds and re-run. Assigned to Tomás to address before enabling nightly job.
decision_log: Prefer minimal fallback envelope over multi-stage recovery to keep SDK handling simple
Assertor implemented outside main runtime to avoid performance risks; runtime instrumentation will remain read-only for this ticket
Treat KV replay collisions as telemetry-classified soft-failures to avoid cascading user-visible schema errors when replay heuristics can correct later
